pr.title: fix(github): catch self-merges/closes via a recently-closed PR sweep
pr.body:
Closes #86. Catch self-merges/closes of your own PRs.

navi missed merges/closes you perform yourself: GitHub never notifies you about your own actions, and the involved-PR sweep was `is:open`, so a PR that already merged had left the search and its transition was never seen. (Diagnosed by dogfooding the 0.2.3 stack merge: only #85 alerted, and only by a race — it merged ~5s before a sweep while GitHub's search index still listed it open.)

### Fix
Add a second involved-PR sweep for recently-**closed** PRs, generalizing the `state=all` + `updated_after` approach already used by the GitLab source (#17):

- `recently_closed_prs`: `is:closed is:pr involves:me updated:>=<cursor>`, bounded by a new `pr_closed_since` cursor (advanced each poll with the standard overlap) so it doesn't rescan history. Second-precision timestamp — GitHub search's `updated:` qualifier rejects subseconds.
- Skipped on the very first poll (no cursor yet) so it baselines forward instead of replaying every old closed PR.
- Both sweeps now share a `diff_swept_prs` helper (search loop extracted to `search_prs`), so there's no duplicated per-PR logic. A closed PR surfaces once on its merge/close bump, diffs against the stored open snapshot, and fires `Merged`/`Closed`. Covers the self-close miss (#21) too.

### Tests
`self_merged_pr_is_caught_by_the_closed_sweep`: open search returns empty (PR already merged), closed search returns the merged PR, and navi fires exactly one `Merged`. Existing involved-PR tests unaffected (closed sweep is skipped without the cursor, i.e. on a first poll).

<!-- git-stk:closes -->
Closes #86
<!-- /git-stk:closes -->

expected.description: The involved-sweep pr: cursor is written before delivery, so a failed send on a closed PR (frozen updated_at) drops the event permanently.

prior_bot.note: flagged eager pr: cursor write for the closed sweep as non-blocking follow-up
